newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo shares sink to 13-month low, Hong Kong up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo shares sink to 13-month low, Hong Kong up.

text.p: Tokyo stocks sagged to close at their lowest level in 13 months on Wednesday amid increasing gloom about Japan's anaemic economy.
Hong Kong shares however, managed modest gains, driven mainly by an upswing in market heavyweight Cheung Kong.
Markets around Asia were generally mixed. Taipei topped the list of gainers with an increase of more than 2 percent, while Tokyo's loss placed it at the other end of the spectrum.
Japan's Nikkei average of 225 leading shares shed 215.81 points or 1.14 percent to close at 18,680.38, its lowest close since November 29, 1995, when it ended at 18,533.98.
Brokers said the slide reflected the market's deepening despondency over government efforts to revive the flagging economy.

Mounting worries over construction firms and financial institutions, which are suffering from bad loan problems, overshadowed the market, they said, as shares in banks, securities firms and construction companies led the nosedive.
Hong Kong stocks ended modestly higher, with gains in Cheung Kong shares and some property counters giving the market a lift but interest rate concerns capped the upside, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed 34.77 points higher at 13,454.93.
"Cheung Kong is doing the whole thing," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities, of the Hang Seng's rise.
Cheung Kong shares ended with a gain of HK$2.00 at HK$74.75.

Taiwan's rally was fired by comments from the island's top securities regulator, who said on Tuesday he was optimistic about the local stock market as the influence of non-economic factors was diminishing.
The weighted price index ended 144.41 points or 2.10 percent higher at 7,019.43 points, the highest since 7,051.49 recorded on January 5, 1995.
Seoul shares also scored strong gains and brokers said sharp rises towards the close were based on talk that the government would soon announce specific market boosting measures.
The composite stock index ended the session 10.36 points or 1.7 percent higher at 621.41.
Thai stocks climbed for the third consecutive trading day, rising 1.44 percent on heavy turnover following a government decision to slash its budget in order to boost the economy, brokers said.
The SET index finished 11.82 points higher to 831.93 on 7.6 billion baht turnover.
Bombay's market closed in positive territory with some stocks surging on active speculative buying, brokers said. The benchmark index rose 23.54 points to end at a provisional 3,287.66.
The Australian share market was buoyed by a resilient performance from Wall Street overnight. The All Ordinaries index climbed 14.3 points to 2,415.0.
Jakarta stocks ended higher in moderate trading after the market shrugged off earlier profit taking with the help of a late burst of buying, traders said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 1.84 points, or 0.28 percent, to close at 662.21 points.
Philippine shares eked out modest gains, lifted by late-session buying on selected blue-chips, brokers said.
The main index ended 11.52 points, or 0.36 percent, higher at 3,206.99.
New Zealand shares ended down with the NZSE-40 capital index slipping 8.97 points to 2,399.31.
